title: Notification Bell
summary: Beeps in your terminal whenever Claude Code asks for permission or waits on you, so an agent that is blocked never sits unnoticed.
description: An agent that waits for a yes can sit idle for an hour. This Notification hook fires whenever Claude Code raises an alert, such as a permission request or a long idle wait, and sounds the terminal bell.
The bell character goes to the terminal device itself, with standard error as a fallback. It does not read the alert text and it never blocks anything.
useWhen: Leave an agent running with approvals on
Know when a permission request is waiting
Stay in another window without missing a prompt
Run several sessions and tell when one needs you

example.prompt: Update the lockfile and run the build.
example.result: Claude asks to run a shell command, the terminal beeps, and you approve it from the other window.

faq.question: How is this different from the Stop bell?
faq.answer: It sounds when Claude needs you, not when it is done. Use both if you want a sound for each.

faq.question: Can I limit it to permission prompts?
faq.answer: Yes. Add a matcher such as permission_prompt to the hook entry in your settings.

access: Writes one bell character to the terminal
